html.question: Which element should contain the primary, unique content of a page?
html.explanation: The main element identifies the document's dominant content and should generally appear once.

html.question: Which attribute connects a label to a form control?
html.explanation: The label's for value must match the control's id to create an explicit accessible association.

html.question: What does the lang attribute on the html element help identify?
html.explanation: A correct language declaration helps assistive technology pronounce content and supports language processing.

html.question: Which element is most appropriate for a self-contained article that could stand on its own?
html.explanation: Article represents self-contained content such as a post, story, or independent entry.

html.question: What is the correct way to provide alternative text for a decorative image?
options: Put the text in the filename
html.explanation: An empty alt tells assistive technology the image is decorative and can be skipped.

html.question: Which element creates a hyperlink to another page?
html.explanation: An anchor with href creates a navigable link. The link element is used for document resources in the head.

html.question: Which input type provides built-in email-format validation?
html.explanation: The email input type provides suitable virtual keyboards and basic built-in format validation.

html.question: Which heading structure is generally best for a page with one main topic and two subtopics?
options: h1 then h2 for each subtopic
Use headings based on visual size
html.explanation: Headings should form a meaningful hierarchy; visual appearance can be styled separately with CSS.

html.question: Which metadata value helps search results summarize a page when selected?
html.explanation: A concise, accurate meta description may be used as a search result snippet, though search engines can choose other text.

html.question:
Which tag is used for the page's main visible heading in this snippet?

Road Safety
html.explanation: The h1 element is a visible heading; title is metadata displayed in browser chrome and often search results.

html.question: Why should a page generally avoid multiple unrelated main elements?
options: It makes the primary content landmark ambiguous
html.explanation: A single main landmark gives assistive technology users a predictable shortcut to the central page content.

html.question: Which attribute makes a button inside a form submit the form by default?
html.explanation: A button's submit type submits its owning form; explicit types avoid accidental submissions for other buttons.

html.question: What is the best link text for a page about CSS Grid?
options: Read the CSS Grid layout guide
html.explanation: Descriptive link text communicates the destination, including when links are encountered out of context.

html.question: What is a key benefit of semantic HTML for search and accessibility?
options: It automatically guarantees a top ranking
It gives content and regions meaningful structure
It replaces the need for text
html.explanation: Semantic elements expose useful content relationships to browsers, assistive technology, and search crawlers.

html.question: Which element should group primary navigation links?
html.explanation: Nav represents a major block of navigation links. Not every collection of links needs a nav landmark.

html.question: What does loading="lazy" on an image generally request?
options: Load the image only after a click
Defer loading until it is near the viewport
html.explanation: Lazy loading can defer off-screen images, reducing initial network work. Avoid lazy-loading important above-the-fold images.

html.question: Which is the strongest reason to include a unique title on every page?
options: It helps users and search engines distinguish pages
html.explanation: A descriptive, page-specific title improves browser tab identification and can inform search result titles.

html.question: When should an image's alt text describe the image's appearance?
options: For every image, regardless of purpose
When the image conveys information not available in nearby text
Only when an image fails to load
html.explanation: Alternative text should convey the image's relevant purpose or information, not repeat nearby content unnecessarily.

html.question: What does a canonical link primarily communicate to search engines?
options: Which URL is the preferred version among duplicates
That the page should never be indexed
html.explanation: Canonical metadata signals the preferred URL for duplicate or substantially similar content; it is a hint, not an absolute directive.

html.question: Why should heading levels not be chosen only for their default font size?
options: Each level has a fixed color
html.explanation: Use heading levels to represent content hierarchy, then style the visual size with CSS.

css.question: What does display: flex establish on an element?
options: A flex formatting context for its children
css.explanation: Flexbox lays out direct children along a main axis and is ideal for one-dimensional alignment.

css.question: Which property adds space between flex or grid items?
css.explanation: The gap property sets spacing between items in flex, grid, and multicol layouts.

css.question: What does box-sizing: border-box do to a declared width?
options: Includes padding and border in the width
css.explanation: With border-box, the declared dimensions include the content, padding, and border.

css.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the root element's font size?
css.explanation: rem is based on the root html element's font size; em is relative to the relevant element context.

css.question: Which rule targets elements with class name card?
css.explanation: A leading dot selects a class. A hash selects an id.

css.question: What does position: relative commonly enable?
options: Offsetting an element from its normal position and anchoring positioned descendants
Removing the element from the DOM
Always placing the element above all others
css.explanation: Relative positioning keeps the element in normal flow while allowing offsets and a containing block for positioned descendants.

css.question: Which selector has higher specificity?
css.explanation: An ID selector has greater specificity than a class, type, or universal selector.

css.question: Which property changes the foreground text color?
css.explanation: The color property sets the foreground color of an element's text and text decorations.

css.question: When is CSS Grid usually a natural choice?
options: When coordinating rows and columns together
css.explanation: Grid is designed for two-dimensional layouts where rows and columns need coordinated sizing.

css.question: Why might z-index: 9999 still appear behind another element?
options: The element may be trapped in a lower stacking context
The browser ignores z-index on all positioned elements
css.explanation: Stacking contexts are independent; a child cannot out-rank elements in a higher ancestor context just by using a larger number.

css.question: Which media query detects a user's reduced-motion preference?
css.explanation: prefers-reduced-motion communicates the user's system-level preference for fewer animations.

css.question: What does grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) create?
css.explanation: It creates three columns that each receive one fraction of the available grid space.

css.question: Which Flexbox property aligns items along the cross axis?
css.explanation: align-items controls cross-axis alignment; justify-content distributes items along the main axis.

css.question: Why use minmax(15rem, 1fr) with repeat(auto-fit, ...)?
options: To create responsive columns with a minimum size
css.explanation: This pattern fits as many columns as possible while keeping each at least 15rem and distributing remaining space.

css.question: Which declaration lets an element's width include padding and border?
css.explanation: border-box makes width and height calculations include padding and border.

css.question: What usually determines which of two equally specific rules wins?
options: The later declaration in source order
css.explanation: When origin, importance, and specificity are otherwise equal, later source order wins.

css.question: Which property can create a stacking context when its value is not none?
css.explanation: A transform other than none creates a stacking context, which can affect z-index relationships.

css.question: A child has z-index: 100 but remains under a sibling. What is the best first debugging step?
options: Inspect ancestor stacking contexts and positioning
Set its z-index to one million immediately
css.explanation: Inspecting ancestor contexts explains the layering boundary; a larger child number cannot cross it.

css.question: What is a key advantage of CSS custom properties?
css.explanation: Custom properties participate in the cascade and can centralize reusable design tokens.

css.question: Which strategy most directly helps avoid layout shift when an image loads?
options: Reserve its space with width/height or aspect-ratio
css.explanation: Reserving the image's dimensions lets the browser allocate space before the file arrives, reducing layout shifts.

javascript.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that should not be reassigned?
javascript.explanation: const prevents rebinding the variable name; object contents can still be mutated unless otherwise controlled.

javascript.question: What does Array.map() return?
options: A new array of transformed values
javascript.explanation: map calls a function for each element and returns a new array containing the callback results.

javascript.question: What is the result of 2 + '3' in JavaScript?
javascript.explanation: With a string operand, + performs concatenation after converting the number to a string.

javascript.question: Which DOM API attaches an event handler without replacing other handlers?
javascript.explanation: addEventListener registers an event listener and allows multiple listeners for the same event.

javascript.question: What does JSON.parse() do?
options: Converts JSON text into a JavaScript value
Converts a value to JSON text
javascript.explanation: JSON.parse parses valid JSON text and can throw a SyntaxError for invalid input.

javascript.question: What is the value of [4, 7].length?
javascript.explanation: The array contains two elements, so its length is 2.

javascript.question: Which operator checks strict equality without type coercion?
javascript.explanation: === compares value and type without coercion; = is assignment and == allows coercion.

javascript.question: What does a function return if it reaches its end without a return statement?
javascript.explanation: A function with no explicit return produces undefined.

javascript.question: What does an async function always return?
javascript.explanation: An async function wraps its return value in a promise; thrown errors become rejected promises.

javascript.question: What does await do inside an async function?
options: Pauses that function until a promise settles
Converts a promise to a callback
javascript.explanation: await suspends the surrounding async function, not the whole JavaScript thread, until the promise settles.

javascript.question: fetch('/api/items') returns a response with status 404. What is true by default?
options: The promise resolves; check response.ok or status
The response body is automatically thrown away
javascript.explanation: fetch rejects for network-level failures, not ordinary HTTP error statuses such as 404.

javascript.question: What does Promise.all() do if any input promise rejects?
options: The returned promise rejects with that failure
javascript.explanation: Promise.all fulfills when all inputs fulfill and rejects as soon as one rejects.

javascript.question: Which is the safest way to render untrusted text into an element?
options: Put it inside a style attribute
javascript.explanation: textContent inserts text rather than parsing it as markup, avoiding a common injection risk.

javascript.question: What does event.preventDefault() do in a form submit handler?
options: Cancels the browser's default submission action
Prevents the event from being created
javascript.explanation: It prevents the default action, such as a form navigation, while other listeners may still run.

javascript.question: In an array filter callback, what does returning false mean for an item?
options: Exclude it from the resulting array
javascript.explanation: filter retains elements for which the callback returns a truthy value.

javascript.question: Which syntax provides a fallback when a value is null or undefined?
javascript.explanation: Nullish coalescing uses the right-hand value only for null or undefined, unlike || which also treats 0 and empty string as falsy.

javascript.question: A promise rejects inside an async function. How can the caller handle it?
options: Use try/catch around await or attach .catch()
A rejected promise cannot be handled
javascript.explanation: Awaited rejection can be handled with try/catch; promise chains can use catch().

javascript.question: What is the output of Promise.resolve(3).then(value => value * 2)?
javascript.explanation: then returns a new promise fulfilled with the callback's return value, here 6.

javascript.question: Why can an event listener on a parent handle clicks from future child elements?
javascript.explanation: Bubbling carries many events from the target toward ancestors, enabling delegation with a target check.

javascript.question: What is a benefit of AbortController with fetch?
options: It can cancel an in-flight request
javascript.explanation: Passing an AbortSignal to fetch allows code to cancel the request, for example when a view is no longer needed.

nodejs.question: What is Node.js primarily used for?
nodejs.explanation: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime commonly used for servers, tooling, and command-line programs.

nodejs.question: In Express, what does app.get('/items', handler) define?
options: A handler for GET requests to /items
nodejs.explanation: The route pairs the GET method and path with the provided request handler.

nodejs.question: Which module provides promise-based file operations in Node.js?
nodejs.explanation: The built-in node:fs/promises module exposes promise-based file-system operations.

nodejs.question: What does npm install express do in a project?
options: Adds Express as a project dependency
nodejs.explanation: npm install adds the package and records it as a dependency in package metadata.

nodejs.question: Which Express middleware parses JSON request bodies?
nodejs.explanation: express.json() parses JSON payloads and makes the result available on req.body.

nodejs.question: What status code commonly indicates a resource was created successfully?
nodejs.explanation: 201 Created indicates the request succeeded and created a resource.

nodejs.question: Where should a private API key be stored for a local Node app?
nodejs.explanation: Secrets belong on the server, typically in environment configuration excluded from version control.

nodejs.question: What should a GET /api/courses route usually do?
options: Return course data without changing it
nodejs.explanation: GET is intended to retrieve a representation and should not perform a state-changing operation.

nodejs.question: Why validate req.body on the server even when the browser validates a form?
nodejs.explanation: Any client can send arbitrary requests, so server-side validation is essential at the trust boundary.

nodejs.question: Which status is suitable when a requested resource does not exist?
nodejs.explanation: 404 Not Found indicates the server has no current representation for the requested resource.

nodejs.question: What is middleware in Express?
options: A function in the request-response pipeline
nodejs.explanation: Middleware can inspect or modify request/response objects, end the response, or pass control onward.

nodejs.question: What does next() commonly do in Express middleware?
options: Pass control to the next middleware or route handler
nodejs.explanation: Calling next() advances through the middleware chain unless an error is passed.

nodejs.question: Which response best fits a malformed or invalid request body?
nodejs.explanation: 400 indicates a client request that the server cannot process because it is invalid.

nodejs.question: Why use a password hash such as bcrypt instead of encryption or plaintext?
options: It is designed to make password guessing computationally expensive
It makes passwords recoverable by admins
It stores passwords in the browser
nodejs.explanation: Password hashing is intentionally one-way and costly to slow offline guessing; plaintext and reversible encryption are not appropriate password storage.

nodejs.question: What does a session cookie marked HttpOnly help prevent?
options: Client-side JavaScript from reading the cookie value
The browser from sending the cookie
nodejs.explanation: HttpOnly prevents scripts from reading the cookie through document.cookie, reducing exposure to some XSS attacks.

nodejs.question: Which Express route handles POST requests to /api/users?
nodejs.explanation: app.post registers a handler for POST requests at the path.

nodejs.question: Why should a production Express app avoid the default in-memory session store?
options: It is not designed for production scale or process restarts
nodejs.explanation: The default store is intended for development; it does not provide robust persistence or multi-instance coordination.

nodejs.question: What should an Express error handler avoid sending to the client in production?
nodejs.explanation: Detailed stack traces can reveal internals and secrets; log details server-side and return a safe message.

nodejs.question: What is the main purpose of rate limiting an expensive API endpoint?
options: Reduce abuse and excessive request volume
nodejs.explanation: Rate limiting bounds request frequency to mitigate abuse and protect availability or paid resources.

nodejs.question: A route awaits a database call that rejects. What is the correct production behavior?
options: Handle the error, log details safely, and send a controlled error response
Ignore it and leave the request open
nodejs.explanation: Asynchronous failures must be handled so the request receives a controlled response and operational details stay in server logs.
